cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Odysseus returns to Ithaca disguised as a beggar by Athena's guidance — he must assess the situation before revealing himself

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Eumaeus the swineherd and Philoetius the cowherd remain loyal to Odysseus and help him against the suitors

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Odysseus and Telemachus plot the suitors' downfall together — father and son are reunited in secret

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Penelope sets the contest of the bow — only Odysseus can string his own great bow and shoot through twelve axes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: The bow contest reveals Odysseus's true identity through his physical superiority and unique skill

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Odysseus, Telemachus, Eumaeus and Philoetius slaughter the suitors in the great hall

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: The loyal servants are spared; the disloyal maidservants who consorted with the suitors are killed

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Penelope tests Odysseus with the secret of their marriage bed — only the true Odysseus would know it cannot be moved

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: The recognition scene (anagnorismos) between Odysseus and Penelope is one of the most famous in literature

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: Odysseus's revenge is brutal but presented as justified by the suitors' violation of xenia

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: The ending of the Odyssey is ambiguous — Athena stops the families of the suitors from seeking further revenge

cards.front: Recall a key point about Homecoming & Revenge
cards.back: The theme of homecoming involves reclaiming not just a place but an identity, a family and a kingdom
